scope: Bibliographic identity and support for the cited statement; not independent proof validation.

references.metadata: Michel Crouzeix and César Palencia. The Numerical Range is a (1+sqrt(2))-Spectral Set. SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 38(2), 649–655 (2017). DOI: 10.1137/17M1116672.
references.content_support: Publisher abstract explicitly says complete (1+sqrt2)-spectral set. The primary paper's complete functional calculus supports the matrix-valued polynomial theorem interface.

references.metadata: Charles R. Johnson. Numerical Determination of the Field of Values of a General Complex Matrix. SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 15(3), 595–602 (June 1978). DOI: 10.1137/0715039.
references.content_support: Primary abstract states boundary points/tangents, convergent computation and an error measure. Official Chebfun also documents the directional Hermitian computation.

references.metadata: Sébastien Loisel and Peter Maxwell. Path-Following Method to Determine the Field of Values of a Matrix with High Accuracy. SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 39(4), 1726–1749 (2018). DOI: 10.1137/17M1148608.
references.content_support: Primary abstract gives an ODE/path-following algorithm, formal error bounds for specific matrix classes and cost-error comparisons. Current prose preserves those restrictions.

references.metadata: Nick Trefethen. Field of values and numerical abscissa. Official Chebfun example, November 2010. Software documentation.
references.content_support: Page expressly attributes the standard method to Johnson (1978) and includes the FOV implementation.

references.metadata: Bernhard Beckermann and Lothar Reichel. Error Estimates and Evaluation of Matrix Functions via the Faber Transform. SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 47(5), 3849–3883 (2009). DOI: 10.1137/080741744.
references.content_support: Primary abstract directly relates Faber transforms on the field of values to improved polynomial Arnoldi and rational Arnoldi error bounds.

references.metadata: Michel Crouzeix and Anne Greenbaum. Spectral Sets: Numerical Range and Beyond. SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 40(3), 1087–1101 (2019). DOI: 10.1137/18M1198417.
references.content_support: Publisher abstract and primary Section 7 explicitly give GMRES and rational Krylov convergence applications.

references.metadata: Youcef Saad and Martin H. Schultz. GMRES: A Generalized Minimal Residual Algorithm for Solving Nonsymmetric Linear Systems. SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing 7(3), 856–869 (July 1986). DOI: 10.1137/0907058.
references.content_support: Primary abstract says residual-norm minimization over a Krylov subspace at each step. The existing corollary is restricted to the exact mathematical method.

references.metadata: Emiel Lorist and Felix L. Schwenninger. A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture. arXiv:2608.03841v2, math.CA. Version 1: 4 August 2026; version 2: 17 August 2026.
references.content_support: Actual HTML Theorem 3 states scalar 2-spectrality for bounded Hilbert-space operators and rational functions with poles outside the numerical-range closure. The manuscript labels this as a preprint assertion and does not infer the complete inequality.

references.metadata: Michel Crouzeix and Anne Greenbaum. Update to: Spectral sets: Numerical range and beyond. arXiv:2609.22460v2, math.NA. Version 1: 18 September 2026; version 2: 23 September 2026.
references.content_support: Actual abstract and text use Lorist–Schwenninger to lower earlier constants, including annular 2-spectral sets and convex regions with circular cutouts. No complete universal claim is attributed.

references.metadata: Michel Crouzeix and Anne Greenbaum. A New Proof that the Numerical Range is a Complete 2-Spectral Set for Weighted Shift Matrices. arXiv:2508.12768v1, math.FA. Version 1: 18 August 2025.
references.content_support: Actual HTML defines the weighted-shift matrix class and gives the completely bounded result. It supports the restricted-class prior-art and sharp-control discussion.

references.metadata: Per Åhag, Rafał Czyż and Jani Virtanen. The Complete Crouzeix Conjecture in Dimension Three and the Clouâtre–Ostermann–Ransford conjecture. arXiv:2608.27346v4, math.CV. Versions: 27 August, 1 September, 9 September, and 21 September 2026.
references.content_support: Actual Theorem 1.1 asserts complete 2-spectrality for base-matrix dimension n <= 3 and arbitrary coefficient size. This directly supports the manuscript's restricted-dimensional claim.

references.classification: AI-produced mathematical preprint with source-supplied corporate authorship
references.metadata: OpenAI (corporate author supplied by the source). A direct proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality. OpenAI Math Release preprint, manuscript dated 26 September 2026. Exact repository commit: adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a.
references.content_support: Actual source main theorem asserts complete constant 2 for positive base/coefficient dimensions and arbitrary polynomial degree, including degenerate numerical ranges. This verifies the attributed claim, not its proof or Lean compilation.

references.metadata: OpenAI. Repository README at commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. The bibliographic title is a descriptive resource label; the actual heading is Readme. Repository documentation.
references.content_support: README says mathematical manuscripts/supporting artifacts come from an internal model and describes mixed verification stages.

references.metadata: OpenAI. The complete Crouzeix conjecture. Lean scope document for family 325 at commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a. Source documentation.
references.content_support: Actual scope text asserts sharp complete constant 2 and lists comparator links. The current paper correctly says scope statement is not an independent compilation report.

references.metadata: Siegfried M. Rump. Verification methods: Rigorous results using floating-point arithmetic. Acta Numerica 19, 287–449 (2010). DOI: 10.1017/S096249291000005X. Published 10 May 2010.
references.content_support: Primary extract directly discusses mathematically rigorous results from computational verification and floating-point arithmetic.

references.metadata: Eitan Tadmor. On the stability of Runge–Kutta methods for arbitrarily large systems of ODEs. Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 78(4), 821–855 (2025). DOI: 10.1002/cpa.22238. First online 20 November 2024; final issue year 2025.
references.content_support: Section 3.2 equations3.3–3.4 directly support the classical numerical-radius power inequality and norm bound; Sections3–5 demonstrate preexisting RK numerical-range stability applications.

metadata.title: Numerical range and functional calculus in Hilbert space

references.verified_content: Publisher abstract explicitly studies polynomial norm bounds involving numerical range and Hilbert-space functional calculus.
Actual paper defines scalar/complete K-spectral constants for convex numerical-range domains and discusses the similarity approach, including complete sharp2for two-dimensional matrices.
references.date_note: Use printed issue year2006, not preprint/online year2005.

metadata.title: Generalization of von Neumann's spectral sets and integral representation of operators
metadata.journal: Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France

references.verified_content: Original publisher and its first page state extension of von Neumann spectral-set theory to numerical ranges through integral representations for nonnormal operators.

metadata.title: Image numérique, GMRES et polynômes de Faber

references.verified_content: Author paper explicitly proves a Faber-polynomial operator norm estimate and derives numerical-range GMRES error estimates; publisher confirms final metadata.

metadata.title: Any Nonincreasing Convergence Curve Is Possible for GMRES
metadata.journal: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications

references.verified_content: Primary abstract gives any prescribed positive nonincreasing GMRES residual sequence with any desired eigenvalues; the proposed nonzero-spectrum sentence is a safe restricted formulation.
references.date_note: The publisher's2012online digitization date is not the article year.

metadata.title: Geometric aspects of the theory of Krylov subspace methods

references.verified_content: Primary abstract treats orthogonal/minimal residual methods as Hilbert-space approximation problems and develops a geometric error analysis.
references.date_note: Use copyright/issue year2001, despite online publication2003.

metadata.title: Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation
metadata.publisher: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics

references.verified_content: Actual publisher chapter excerpts discuss polynomial/contour matrix functions, applications, conditioning and Fréchet derivatives, including a dedicated f(A)b chapter.
references.date_note: 2008book year, not2012online digitization. Print/electronic ISBNs differ; proposed entry avoids mixing them.

metadata.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms
metadata.publisher: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics

references.verified_content: Publisher chapters1–3 treat forward/backward errors, conditioning and finite arithmetic; chapter5 is explicitly Polynomials, pp93–104.
references.date_note: Keep second edition2002rather than later digital appearance.

metadata.title: Theory of Inexact Krylov Subspace Methods and Applications to Scientific Computing

references.verified_content: Primary abstract supplies a framework and computable criteria for matrix-vector inexactness assuming exact arithmetic in the analysis. The proposed sentence does not claim a universal validated floating-point solver.

Primary abstract gives rigorous sufficient tests for Hermitian positive definiteness via floating-point Cholesky with rounding errors and underflow included. It supports strict support validation, not a blanket test for singular semidefiniteness.

metadata.title: Computing the Action of the Matrix Exponential, with an Application to Exponential Integrators

references.verified_content: Primary abstract specifies scaling and truncated Taylor polynomials, backward-error tolerance, power-norm quantities and exponential-integrator applications. This is prior application motivation, not evidence that our prototype implements that algorithm.

metadata.title: A Block Algorithm for Matrix 1-Norm Estimation, with an Application to 1-Norm Pseudospectra
metadata.journal: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications

references.verified_content: Original published Section5 explicitly calls the computed estimate a lower bound. It therefore supports a concrete caution that an estimator needs separate upper validation before serving as c_j in a norm certificate.

metadata.title: Partial Smoothness of the Numerical Radius at Matrices Whose Fields of Values are Disks
metadata.journal: SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications

references.verified_content: Published article equation1.1 explicitly states ||A^k||2<=2r(A)^k, with complex unit vectors in W(A); page1005attributes the older proofs to Berger and Pearcy. Final metadata now checked, superseding the round1unverified publication-data limit.
Original78-page paper discusses construction, analysis, implementation and applications of exponential integrators, including matrix functions applied to vectors and spatially discretized problems.
